clues: It is a city in the Aegean part of Turkey, and the seat of its own province. Think of the side of Turkey that faces the blue Aegean Sea.
Summers here are hot, but winters can turn very cold. Snow falls on the hills round the town, and some years it snows in town too.
In the first years AD, a town named Colossae stood just west of here. Ruins of two more old towns still lie close by today.
A hill near town wears a thick coat of stone from a hot spring. Crowds come from far to see it and rest at spa inns near by.
This town shares its fame with Pamukkale, the hot-spring hill close by. One of its own core wards bears that same famed name.
